segments: The wife of the Caliph was with Quraysh.
And when Sultan Tughril sent an envoy and asked for her,
they sent her to him with great honors.
And in this year died the Emir Da'ud Chaghri Beg, the brother of Sultan Tughril,
and he left an eldest son,
Alp Arslan,
and two other sons.
And the Sultan sent an envoy to Quraysh and thanked him concerning Arslan Khatun,
that he had kept her in honor and sent her [back].
And he said to him:
"I desire that you also restore the Caliph to his throne,
and you shall be his administrator.
And I will not come again to Baghdad,
but I will occupy myself with the administration of the kingdom of Persia.
And if you are unable on account of al-Basasiri, who does not comply with your will,
it is fitting that in one of the fortresses or in the desert you fortify your precious self and your people,
lest, when our armies come,
they unwittingly harm anyone belonging to you.
For a great obligation has become due to you from us,
and even if we were to give you everything we have,
[it would be] less than that which you gave us,
in that you returned our child to us safely."
Then Quraysh sent to al-Basasiri, who was in Wasit:
"Why and for whom are we fighting all this fight? For the sake of the Egyptian [Caliph],
who has not visited us even with a simple letter,
in return for our having championed his proclamation even in Baghdad? Rather, it is fitting for us to come to terms with the Sultan,
and restore the Caliph again to his place."
And when al-Basasiri would not be persuaded by him,
that Quraysh took what belonged to him and set out for the desert.
And the Sultan and his armies drew near to the border of Baghdad.
And the Emir of Haditha,
with whom the Caliph was imprisoned,
brought him to the Sultan.
And the Sultan sent him back again to his palace with great honor,
and made an apology to him:
"Because of the death of my brother Chaghri Beg and the settlement of his sons,
and on account of my other brother Ibrahim, who rebelled against me,
I was delayed from [coming to] you."
And with such words he comforted the Caliph.
And he sent an army against al-Basasiri,
and he was defeated.
And as he was fleeing,
the Ghuzz overtook him,
and they cut off his head and brought it to the Sultan.
And he commanded, and it was fixed upon the head of a lance,
and hung up at the gate of the palace.
